headlines.title: IBM (IBM) Lands $1 Billion Quantum Foundry Award And Deepens AI Oversight
headlines.summary: International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) said its subsidiary Anderon won a US$1b federal award to build a U.S. quantum chip foundry, alongside a further US$1b IBM commitment to the project. The planned facility is described as the first stand-alone quantum wafer foundry in the U.S., focused on quantum chip manufacturing under CHIPS Act funding.

headlines.title: IBM (IBM) Stock Could Trade At A Discount On AI Governance News
headlines.summary: International Business Machines has given long term holders a strong run over the past few years, yet after a sharp setback this year the question now is whether the current US$237.75 share price still lines up with the cash it is expected to generate. Recent headlines around quantum computing, AI governance and a major investigation into a recent earnings shortfall have further sharpened the focus on what IBM’s cash flows are really worth.

headlines.title: Is IBM Stock Riskier Than Its Options Market Now Assumes?
headlines.summary: International Business Machines (IBM) shares trade near $237, and options price a one-year range around that from $161.75 to $348.69. That band is the calmer version of this stock. Over the past year IBM moved harder than its options now assume. The business question hanging over IBM comes from the second quarter of 2026: whether the software deals that slipped were delayed or lost.

headlines.title: IBM Secures $1 Billion Commerce Award as Quantum Foundry Starts Production
headlines.summary: A $1 billion federal award doubles disclosed funding, but contracted wafer demand remains unknown.

headlines.title: Dun & Bradstreet Brings Verified Business Context to IBM watsonx Orchestrate Through MCP
headlines.summary: Dun & Bradstreet today announced that the D&B Commercial Graph™ is now available in the IBM watsonx Orchestrate Agent Catalog via Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The integration helps organizations move from AI prototypes to production-ready agentic workflows by providing secure access to verified business identity, relationships, and context.

description: International Business Machines Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides integrated solutions and services in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. It operates through Software, Consulting, Infrastructure, and Financing segments. The Software segment offers hybrid cloud and AI platforms that allow clients to realize their digital and AI transformations across the applications, data, and environments in which they operate. The Consulting segment delivers strategy and technology services and intelligent operations, providing business transformation, technology implementation, managed services, application modernization, and AI-powered solutions. The Infrastructure segment provides on-premises and cloud-based server, and storage solutions, as well as life-cycle services for hybrid cloud infrastructure deployment. The Financing segment offers client and commercial financing, and facilitates IBM clients' acquisition of hardware, software, and services. It operates a data streaming platform. The company has strategic partnerships with various companies, including hyperscalers, service providers, global system integrators, and software and hardware vendors that include Adobe, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, Samsung Electronics and SAP, and others. It also has a strategic collaboration with Arm Holdings plc for the development of new dual-architecture hardware that helps enterprises run future AI and data intensive workloads; strategic partnership with three.ws to advance ai-powered 3d agent technology; and collaboration with Lightwell to help strengthen open source software supply chain. Additionally, it offers operational resilience, logistics, and future-ready technology to the UK Ministry of Defence through Team ORION. The company was formerly known as Computing-Tabulating-Recording Co. and changed its name to International Business Machines Corporation in 1924. International Business Machines Corporation was incorporated in 1911 and is headquartered in Armonk, New York.
